sources.claim: UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity for Russia (June 2025) is the national framework this division is scored against: consensual same-sex activity is not criminalised, but same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned; the Supreme Court designated the international LGBT+ movement an 'extremist' organisation in November 2023; between 2022 and 2024 at least 139 individuals were affected by anti-LGBT+ law enforcement, with 'gay propaganda' fines up to 400,000 rubles (about £3,600) or 15 days' detention for individuals, and trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023. The note contains no division-specific information beyond that national framework.

Human Rights Watch (30 June 2025): Russian courts have issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions for participation in the 'International LGBT Movement' or displaying its symbols since the Supreme Court's November 2023 designation, with defendants facing up to 12 years in prison; HRW also documented 81 people found guilty in 98 cases since January 2024 of administrative offences (article 20.3) for displaying banned LGBT symbols, mostly on social media. This national enforcement baseline underpins the national score this division is assessed at; the article contains no division-specific detail.

sources.claim: UK Home Office country policy and information note on SOGI for Russia (June 2025), the national framework this division is scored against, carries one division-specific enforcement datapoint: a Novosibirsk court fined the Elton John Bar 500,000 rubles (about £4,598) for 'promoting LGBTI propaganda' through a rainbow flag, following the bar's appearance in a video by LGBT+ activist blogger Karen Shainyan. Nationally, same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned, the Supreme Court designated the international LGBT+ movement 'extremist' in November 2023, and 2022-2024 enforcement affected at least 139 people (individual 'gay propaganda' fines up to 400,000 rubles, about £3,600, or 15 days' detention). The note also quotes a priest from a village in the Novosibirsk region telling The Moscow Times that religion can correct 'deviations', as context on local attitudes.

This national enforcement baseline underpins the national score this division is assessed at; the article contains no division-specific detail.

records.name: Smolensk Oblast
records.current_summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which found no region-specific trans-related evidence for it: hostility here is legislated federally and administered by federal security services, so the division inherits the national picture (score 0.12; deviation vs national ±0.02). The federal layer applying here: the 2023 ban on legal gender recognition and gender-affirming care; the propaganda law (up to 15 days' detention plus deportation for foreign visitors who 'promote' non-traditional relationships); the 'LGBT extremism' designation regime (101 convictions, 146 fines in 2024); and uncorrectable document markers, so any police, hotel or transport identity check reads a mismatch.
